transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello Doctor, I'm Phu. My family says I’m always getting sidetracked and forgetting what I was supposed to be doing, which has them worried about my memory. My primary care doctor suggested this evaluation after I missed another appointment, though I still feel pretty sharp in conversation.
Have you struggled with these difficulties with focus and organization since you were a child, or is this a relatively new change that has developed recently?

While it has gotten much more noticeable over the past year since I retired and took on more tasks, these struggles actually go all the way back to my childhood. Even in primary school, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was always daydreaming, missing instructions, and forgetting to bring home the right books. It has just become a bigger issue lately because I have more to manage.
Did you ever receive a formal diagnosis or treatment for these attention difficulties when you were younger, or were you able to manage them reasonably well until your recent retirement?

No, I never received any formal diagnosis or treatment back then; I just managed to get by on my own despite my teachers' comments. It was only after I retired and took on so many unstructured commitments over the past year that these long-standing difficulties became a real problem and led me here.
Besides having trouble with focus, do you often find yourself feeling restless, having difficulty sitting still, or acting without thinking?

Yes, I definitely struggle with feeling restless inside. During long meetings or in waiting rooms, I'm constantly shifting in my seat and looking for an excuse to stand up, and my legs get too fidgety for quiet things like reading. I don't really notice acting without thinking, but sitting still is definitely a big challenge for me.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others while they are speaking or blurting out answers before a question is finished?

No, I don't really interrupt others or blurt things out. My issue in conversations is actually the opposite, where my mind will drift off while the other person is talking and I end up missing what they just said.
Looking back at your childhood, do you recall frequently running around, climbing on things, or feeling 'driven by a motor' even when you were expected to sit still?

No, I don't recall being physically hyperactive or running around and climbing on things like that as a kid. My difficulties back in school were much more about daydreaming, missing instructions, and forgetting to bring home the right books. I could still answer questions just fine once the teachers actually got my attention, though.
Besides the restlessness you mentioned, do you often find that you lose or misplace important items like your keys, wallet, or phone on a frequent basis?

Yes, absolutely, I do that all the time. I'm constantly walking around the house patting my pockets and asking my wife if she's seen my glasses, keys, or phone. I'll just set them down for a second while I'm doing something, and then I have no idea where I left them.
